title: Why Businesses in Nepal Must Separate Personal & Business Finances
metaDescription: Discover why commingling personal and company funds in Nepal exposes owners to severe tax audits, piercing of the corporate veil, and banking friction.
h1: Why Businesses Should Separate Personal and Business Finances
directAnswer: Businesses in Nepal must strictly separate personal and commercial finances to protect limited liability under the Companies Act 2063, prevent disqualification of deductible business expenses during Inland Revenue Department (IRD) audits, ensure accurate bank loan evaluations, and maintain clear accounting records necessary for annual statutory audit clearance.
author: Lalitpur Advisory Research Desk

sections.h2: The Dangers of Commingling Funds in Nepal
sections.contentHtml:
In family-owned enterprises and early-stage startups in Nepal, founders frequently use personal bank accounts (or QR payment scanners linked to personal accounts) for business receipts. This creates severe compliance and operational perils:

  • Piercing the Corporate Veil: Under Companies Act 2063, a Private Limited company is a separate legal person. Commingling funds destroys limited liability protection, making directors personally liable for company debts.
  • Disallowed Tax Expenses at IRD: The Inland Revenue Department strictly disallows expense deductions paid from personal non-business accounts without proper tax vouchers and invoice records.
  • Rejection of Commercial Bank Loans: Credit analysts at commercial banks require clean, company-titled audited bank statements. Personal transaction clutter invalidates bankable loan feasibility models.
  • Director Loan Complications: Transferring money between personal and corporate accounts without board resolutions creates deemed dividend or unauthorized loan compliance liabilities under Income Tax Act Section 88.

1. Open Dedicated Corporate Bank Accounts: Direct all customer payments exclusively into bank accounts registered under the company's legal name and PAN.
  2. Deploy Commercial Merchant QRs: Replace personal Fonepay/eSewa QR stands with merchant QR codes tied to your corporate account.
  3. Pay Directors via Formal Salary or Dividends: Never withdraw ad-hoc cash from company accounts for personal groceries; pay a fixed monthly salary with appropriate TDS deducted.
  4. Issue Corporate Expense Cards: Provide designated corporate cards with receipt-submission mandates for executive travel.

faqs.question: Can I pay company expenses from my personal card and reimburse myself?
faqs.answer: Yes, provided the original VAT tax invoice is made out to the company's legal name and PAN, and a formal reimbursement voucher is filed with accounting.
